description: Reading an unbound mixed-case `:SomeVar` raises `ol-undefined-var` whose `params.name` is the case-insensitive resolution identity `somevar`, NOT the source casing — so the runtime guard agrees with the semantic checker's folded `params.name` for the same condition (issue #1005). Variable resolution folds case (`lookupVar`), so one condition must have one diagnostic identity (`spec/error-model.md:255-260`). Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists, but it runs only under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — NOT in this fixture, which is checked — and when it does run it is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why the runtime's copy never appears beside the check's. So nothing here observes that copy, and reading this fixture as evidence for it would be a mistake: measured, a runtime guard can be deleted outright with the whole conformance corpus still green, because the surviving report is the check's either way. What the runtime copy uniquely contributes is that the run STOPS at the fault, which is written in the event stream rather than in the diagnostics and is pinned by `packages/runtime/src/runtime-guards-halt.test.mjs`.
